key_source_quotes: The Air Toxics "Hot Spots" Information and Assessment Act ... requires stationary sources to report the types and quantities of certain substances routinely released into the air.

A facility is subject to the Act if it: (1) manufactures, formulates, uses, or releases a substance subject to the Act ... and emits 10 tons or more per year of total organic gases, particulate matter, nitrogen oxides or sulfur oxides; (2) is listed in any district's existing toxics use or toxics air emission survey, inventory or report ...; or (3) manufactures, formulates, uses, or releases a substance subject to the Act ... and emits less than 10 tons per year of criteria pollutants and is subject to emission inventory requirements.
Facility operators must submit to the district a proposed emission inventory plan indicating how emissions will be measured or calculated.
missing_facts: whether facility is on district toxics inventory or subject to district emission inventory/source category requirements

summary: Potentially applicable / unresolved. CARB states AB 2588 requires stationary sources to report types and quantities of certain substances routinely released into air. A coating/paint shop storing/using solvent could involve listed toxic substances and routine releases, but AB 2588 applicability is administered through local air districts and depends on listed-substance use/release plus criteria-pollutant emissions, district toxics inventory/emission-inventory status, or source-category requirements. CARB’s overview says a facility is subject if it manufactures, formulates, uses, or releases a subject substance and emits 10 tons/year or more of specified criteria pollutants; is listed in any district toxics use/emission survey, inventory, or report; or uses/releases a subject substance with less than 10 tons/year criteria pollutants and is subject to emission inventory requirements. Because the input lacks county/air-district and emissions/VOC composition facts, determine the controlling district and solvent constituents/VOC emissions before concluding whether an AB 2588 inventory plan/report, risk assessment, notification, risk reduction plan, or fees are required.
title: H-AIR-AB2588 — California AB 2588 Air Toxics “Hot Spots” applicability cannot be finally resolved without the facility’s local air district
